51#main: How are they equal in bringing and delivering? One who brings a release document in Eretz Yisrael need not say before written and before signed; in chutz la'aretz, if witnesses to authenticate are not found and the agent said before written and before signed — this is authentication; and if the master came afterward and protested, we pay no attention.
52#main: Just as a woman brings her get and need not authenticate it since the get leaves her hand, so a slave whose release document leaves his hand need not authenticate it.
53#main: And just as a woman says before written and before signed if so conditioned, so the slave.
54#main: Whoever is fit to bring a woman's get is fit to bring a slave's release document.
55#main: A slave accepts a get for his fellow from his fellow's master, but not from his own master.
56#main: One who gives a release document to a slave on condition he be freed in court — whether written yourself and acquired property is yours, or all my property is acquired for you — he acquires himself by his saying before written and before signed; property he does not acquire until authenticated by signatories.
57#main: One who writes all his property to his slave — he goes out to freedom, for he is included in the property and acquires himself included in property; but if he reserved some property, land or movable, whether he specified the reservation or not, whether he had other property besides what he reserved or not — even if he wrote yourself and all my acquired property is yours except such-and-such item — he does not go out to freedom and does not acquire property.
58#main: One who writes a betrothal document to his maidservant — even if he said to her go out with it to freedom and be betrothed with it — this is not language of release; she is neither betrothed nor freed (there chapter 6 of Laws of Slaves): {Rama: (But if he said be betrothed with it alone, we say he certainly freed her from the start and betrothal took effect) (Beit Yosef in the name of Rashi, and so Gemara chapter HaSholeach).}
59#main: One who frees two slaves in one document — they did not acquire themselves; therefore one who writes all his property to two slaves in one document — even themselves they did not acquire; and if he wrote two documents they acquire and free each other. When do we say this? When he wrote in each document all my property is given to so-and-so my slave: {Rama: (and gave both documents to one person together) (Tur).} But if he wrote half my property to so-and-so my slave and half to so-and-so my slave — even in two documents they acquired nothing.
60#main: One who frees half his slave by document — the slave did not acquire his half and remains a slave as he was; but if he freed half with money the slave gave him half his value to free himself — he acquired and is half free. When do we say this? When he freed half by document and the other half remained; but if he sold or gave him to another, whether release and sale or gift together or sale or gift preceded release — the slave acquired his half and the buyer or recipient has the other half; and likewise a slave of two partners — if one freed his share, even by document, he acquired and is half free.
61#main: One who writes to his pregnant maidservant, behold you are a free daughter and your child is a slave — his words stand regarding her and your child is a free son — he said nothing.
62#main: One who is half slave half free cannot marry a maidservant or free woman; therefore they compel his master to free him and write a document on half his value; and before writing the bill of release, his labor is for himself; and if his ox killed a person he does not pay: {Rama: neither fine nor kofer.} When do we say this? For a male slave because he is commanded regarding procreation; but a maidservant remains as she was — works for herself one day and her master one day; and if a person struck her hand and it withered and will return — if struck on the day she works for her master, damage to master; if on her day, damage to herself; but if her hand was cut off or anything that will not return — they divide damage between her and master; and if she killed, he gives half the fine to master and is exempt from half kofer.
63#main: A slave of two partners — if one freed his share, they compel the second also to free his share; and if he knew his fellow wished to free his share and gave his share to his minor son and afterward his fellow freed — beit din cannot compel the minor to free; but they appoint a guardian, appraise the slave, give part of the value to the minor so he agrees to free, and the guardian frees him with money the minor received and writes a bill of release in his name — specifically when intending to uproot the Sages' enactment; but if he died leaving a minor and afterward the partner freed his share — they do not appoint a guardian to free for the minor, but he works for himself one day and the minor one day until he grows up.
64#main: One who declares his slave ownerless — he goes out to freedom and needs a bill of release; and if the master died before freeing him, the heir writes him a bill of release.
65#main: A convert who died without heirs and had adult slaves — they acquired themselves and are free; minors have no power to acquire themselves, and whoever precedes acquires them: {Rama: (And if no one acquired them until they grew, they have no remedy) (Tur in the name of R' Meir of Rothenburg).}
66#main: A slave who was captured and escaped — if another came after his master despaired of him, he cannot be enslaved again; and they compel him to write a bill of release.
67#main: A captured slave — if his first master despaired of him, whoever redeems him for slavery may enslave him and he is his; if redeemed for freedom, behold he is free; and if the first master did not despair — one who redeems for slavery takes redemption from the master and returns to the master; if redeemed for freedom, returns to first master for nothing.
68#main: A slave his master made collateral for his creditor and afterward freed him — his servitude is uprooted and behold he is free; and he must pay the creditor; and they compel the creditor to write him a bill of release.
69#main: An Israelite who had relations with a maidservant — even his own maidservant — the child is a slave; and some say if with his maidservant or he consecrated her, the child is free for all matters (Rav Neturai Gaon, Rosh, and see): {Rama: And some say that for other matters he is like free but not permitted to an Israelite woman until he receives a bill of release.}
70#main: A slave whose master married him to an Israelite woman (and all the more if he marries his maidservant) (Tur), or the master put tefillin on his head, or the master told him to read three verses from a Torah scroll before the congregation, and all similar matters one is obligated in only as a free person — he goes out to freedom and they compel the master to write a bill of release; but if he borrowed from his slave, or made him a guardian, or put tefillin before his master, or read three verses before his master in congregation (or married an Israelite woman before him) (Tur), and the master did not protest — he does not go out to freedom.
71#main: Forbidden to teach one's slave Torah; and if he taught him, he does not go out to freedom.
72#main: Some say a slave who vowed a vow they can compel him to transgress, such as vowed not to eat meat and the like, and his master said I permit you — he goes out to freedom, for since he did not compel him where he could compel, he revealed intent to uproot his servitude.
73#main: One who frees his slave in any language and uttered words implying no servitude remains at all and resolved in his heart for this — he cannot retract; and they compel him to write a bill of release.
74#main: If he wrote in a document I will make so-and-so my slave a free man and gave to his hand — he does not go out to freedom; but if he wrote I made so-and-so my slave a free man, or he is made a free man, or behold he is a free man, or he shall be a free man, and gave to his hand — he goes out to freedom; but if he said orally one of these formulas — he does not go out to freedom. And this is when healthy; but a deathly ill person who said one of these formulas — he goes out to freedom and needs a bill of release to permit him to an Israelite woman; and they compel heirs to write for him; and even when healthy, if they said as admission, he goes out to freedom and needs a bill of release and they compel the master to write for him.
75#main: One who says I made so-and-so my slave a free man and he says he did not make me — we are concerned perhaps he transferred merit through another; but if he said I wrote a bill of release and gave it to him and he says he did not write or give — admission of a litigant is like a hundred witnesses and behold he is a slave: {Rama: [And if the master returned and said he did not give it] the slave cannot return and say I received it; and if the master stands by his word, they compel him to write a bill of release (Tur in the name of R' Meir of Rothenburg).}
